# Kurambit

> Kurambit is an open-source desktop app for making games with the coding agent you already use. You describe a game; your agent builds it, a separate tester session plays every build, a judge compares each new build blind against the one before it, and only builds that come out better are kept. A run keeps going until its budget ends, so a game can keep improving overnight.

Kurambit is open source under the MIT license and is currently invite-only: people join a waitlist on kurambit.com and are let in in small batches.

## What it works with

- Coding agents: Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode and Antigravity, plus any agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). One signed-in agent is enough for the whole loop.
- Engines and tools: games are built in Godot, with art made in Blender. Kurambit installs both.
- Platform: Linux on x86_64 today.

## What you get

- Any genre. One brief aims for a game shaped like a Steam demo: something you can play, judge and keep improving.
- Every game is its own git repository on your machine, with a normal Godot project and the Blender files that made its art. It opens without Kurambit.
- You can direct it in plain words at any time; the next round takes the request on, and nothing reaches you until it beats the build before it.

## Cost

Kurambit is free and open source. It runs on the agent subscription you already pay for.
